text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: private-controlplane-vpc-connectivity -> P1. Trigger: control-plane-heartbeat-missing for customer ACME-VPC-7. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/private-controlplane-vpc

pagerduty: page fired to schedule: oncall-rotation-1 (maria). Escalation in 5m if unacked.

maria (oncall): Acked. I'm looking. first-pass: check control plane health and agent heartbeats.

ops-bot: Recent events: agent-heartbeat-missed x3 (hosts: onprem-agent-12, onprem-agent-13, onprem-agent-14), last seen 1710503500. Control plane API 502 from customer VPC NAT.

maria (oncall): Copy. Running quick checks:
```
# from control-plane console
curl -sS https://private-controlplane.acme-vpc.internal/health || true
ssh -i /secrets/acme-deploy-key ops@onprem-agent-12 "sudo systemctl status redwood-agent"
traceroute -n 10.2.0.1
```

maria (oncall): curl -> timeout. SSH to agent-12 fails (no route). traceroute shows last hop 10.2.0.1 (customer edge) dropping. Looks like customer edge NAT/router not forwarding to agents.

sasha: I can ping the peering tunnel metrics from our side, traffic counters show flapping on the VPN tunnel between acl-prod-us-east and acme-vpc-7 starting ~1710503400.

maria (oncall): Good catch. That explains NATs. Reached out to ACME infra (acct: acme-enterprise) via support channel and their on-call (cc @acme-netops). Asking them to check edge router and BGP.

maria (oncall): Mitigation options:
- If tunnel comes up quickly, we recover automatically.
- If prolonged, we can switch the customer's private deployment to fallback public-control-plane (pre-approved emergency fallback). That requires a ticket and brief config change, data plane will flow via encrypted overlay.

tj: If we flip to public fallback we should warn them about IP rerouting and confirm no private-only compliance blockers. Do we have approval from account team?

maria (oncall): I paged account lead (sasha-sales) and legal-sig channel. Waiting consent. ACME had emergency fallback in signed SOW but we need their explicit ack to proceed.

ops-bot: Incident severity suggestion: keep P1 until agents return or fallback initiated. Noting customer SLA: Dedicated private: 99.95, impacted.

maria (oncall): Timeline so far:
- 1710503400: tunnel flapping begins
- 1710503500: agents missed heartbeat
- 1710503600: PagerDuty page fired (this thread)

sasha: ACME netops replied in support: "We're seeing high CPU on edge router, restarting control-plane NAT process now. ETA 10-15m."

maria (oncall): Good. I'll monitor. Meanwhile, let's gather logs in case restart fails. Asking ops to capture netflow / tcpdump at egress.

sasha: Starting tcpdump on our peering host: `sudo tcpdump -i eth1 host 10.2.0.1 and port 443 -w /tmp/acme-edge.pcap`

maria (oncall): Also requested them to run `show ip route` and `show bgp summary`.

(5m later)

pagerduty: escalation: oncall not escalated (acked by maria).

maria (oncall): Update: ACME confirms router process restart succeeded, tunnel reports up at 1710504100. Agents are re-registering.

ops-bot: agent-heartbeat restored: onprem-agent-12 (1710504152), onprem-agent-13 (1710504201), onprem-agent-14 (1710504228). Control plane API healthy.

maria (oncall): Verified health endpoints: `curl -sS https://private-controlplane.acme-vpc.internal/health` -> {"status":"ok","agents":3}. Rolling checks on metrics dashboard show no error spike in the last 5m.

tj: Nice. Any postmortem action items?

maria (oncall): Drafting initial RCA: root cause likely buggy NAT process on customer edge causing tunnel BGP flapping and drop of inbound connections. Action items:
- ACME: schedule edge-router firmware update + investigate process leak (assigned to acme-netops).
- Redwood: add monitoring alert for peering tunnel flaps (SLO: detect >3 flaps in 10m) and a runbook step to surface fallback opt-in earlier.
- Support: confirm fallback opt-in documented in account record.

sasha: Adding: add a synthetic heartbeat probe from our peering host to agent endpoints to catch these before control plane metrics degrade.

maria (oncall): Agree. I'll open post-incident ticket and assign to eng-infra for monitoring rule.

maria (oncall): Handoff: I'm going offline for 30m, leaving incident in monitoring state. tj, can you take over as incident lead for follow-up and track postmortem?

tj: I'll take. I'll consolidate logs and start postmortem doc. tagging eng-infra and support.

maria (oncall): Thanks — marking page resolved for now. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: PagerDuty: incident resolved (auto) at 1710504800.

tj: Will update incident tracker and draft timeline. Anyone else with notes, paste here.

sasha: Saved pcap to /var/tmp/acme-edge-1710504100.pcap and uploaded to the incident share.

maria (oncall): Great job team.

(End of thread)
